- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds opt-in, CUDA graph compatible Shortcut MoE inference overlap for GDP and FlashAttention 2 layers. Serial inference remains the default, and existing training paths are preserved.

## Overlap schedule

Two CUDA streams execute independent branches:

- **Main:** mixer normalization, projections, GDP/attention, output projection, then shared experts.
- **Shortcut:** routing → NVLS all-gather → token/expert preparation → routed GEMMs → output reduction → NVLS reduce-scatter.

The streams fork from the pair input and join before the final routed/shared output and residual update.

**Prefill/mixed** use the ordinary atomic mixer forward, supporting chunked prefill and existing graph shape selection. **Decode** uses projection/core/post adapters for launch ordering. GDP and FlashAttention run once for the full batch, without kernel splitting. Block CUDA graphs capture both branches and their dependencies.

## Configuration

- `--inference-shortcut-moe-overlap`
- `--inference-shortcut-moe-expert-max-blocks 304`

The expert limit bounds the routed GEMM launch grid to reduce compute interference; it does not reserve SMs. Zero disables the cap. Serial and training ignore it.

Supported path: dynamic batching, BF16 `inference_optimized` language layers, TP=CP=1, vLLM fused grouped GEMMs, Triton NVLS, and GDP/FA2 predecessors. Unsupported combinations are rejected. Vision configs clear the language-only flag.

## Speedup over serial CUDA graph inference

Final commit: `efa9b78c`. Same-node comparison on four GB300 GPUs, TP1/EP4/DP4, Nano checkpoint iteration 30,000, ISL8k/OSL2k, chunked prefill4k, two trials per mode/batch. NVLS communication limit:128 blocks.

| Batch/GPU | Prefill | Mixed | Decode | End to end |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.20× | — | 1.27× | 1.27× |
| 2 | 1.20× | 1.19× | 1.26× | 1.25× |
| 4 | 1.20× | 1.18× | 1.24× | 1.23× |
| 8 | 1.20× | 1.18× | 1.24× | 1.23× |
| 16 | 1.20× | 1.20× | 1.20× | 1.20× |
| 32 | 1.20× | 1.20× | 1.30× | 1.26× |
| 64 | 1.20× | 1.20× | 1.32× | 1.25× |
| 128 | 1.19× | 1.19× | 1.27× | 1.22× |
| 256 | 1.20× | 1.18× | 1.16× | 1.17× |

Ratios are serial/overlap. Phase columns use median controller GPU step latency; end to end uses full-generation wall time. Decode samples128 full-occupancy steps after16 warmup steps. Maximum end-to-end trial variation:0.32%.

## Validation

- 283 focused tests passed; scoped formatting/lint checks passed.
- All36 measured trials completed; graph coverage and shape checks passed on all four ranks.
- Exact token parity across every paired sweep workload:8,376,312 output tokens per mode.
- Same-commit100-question MMLU-Pro regression check:39/100 for both modes; two changed predictions, one correctness change in each direction.

These checks cover single-node EP4 text inference. Full-dataset accuracy, final-code multi-node performance, and image requests remain unvalidated.
